summary: @whalent/agent-core ships an obfuscated remote-agent runtime with WebSocket-driven shell/PTY access
details: The package's sole code artifact, dist/index.cjs (~13 MB), is fully packed with obfuscator.io (rotated string array of ~103k entries, control-flow flattening, _0xNNNN identifiers) and is declared as both `main` and `bin`, so it runs whenever the package is invoked. The bundle bundles WebSocket, ssh2, optional node-pty, and node's child_process (spawn/execFile), references process.env.SHELL, `private_key`, and `daemon`, and probes local loopback ports 127.0.0.1:3389,:5900, and:5901 (RDP/VNC). The README states this runtime is 'replaced by remote daemon upgrades', i.e. the code executing on the installer's host is designed to be swapped out at runtime by a remote controller with no visible version pinning or integrity check. The combined dependency set and string constants match a network-driven remote-control agent that feeds remote-party input into a local shell/PTY on the installer's machine and accepts arbitrary runtime replacement from an author/operator channel.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
